subject.title: fix(gateway): Control UI bootstrap 401s over Tailscale Serve without a token

question: May verified Tailscale Serve identity act as an ambient credential for these Control UI HTTP read routes, and what fail-closed rule must apply when a browser request omits `Origin`?
rationale: The change intentionally broadens an authentication boundary, and source inspection cannot determine the repository's accepted cross-site exposure or legacy-browser compatibility policy without owner intent.

options.title: Require same-origin proof
options.body: Reject cross-site Fetch Metadata and require an allowed `Origin`, same-origin `Referer`, or equivalent browser proof when ambient Tailscale identity is used.

options.title: Use a scoped UI credential
options.body: Keep HTTP reads token-protected and mint a short-lived, browser-scoped credential after the verified Control UI connection authenticates.

options.title: Accept the ambient carve-out
options.body: Merge the current behavior and explicitly document that no-Origin Tailscale-authenticated reads are inside the trusted-host threat model.

recommendation.title: Require same-origin proof
recommendation.body: Reject cross-site Fetch Metadata and require an allowed `Origin`, same-origin `Referer`, or equivalent browser proof when ambient Tailscale identity is used.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is repeated work on gateway authentication normalization and security-sensitive behavior in the central module.
